cf.title: Fix cumulative WAL statistics double-counting from parallel workers

input.subject: Fix cumulative WAL statistics double-counting from parallel workers

verdict_reasoning: The bug is real and reproduced in message #1 and message #22, and no objection survived at level 1a or 1b. The surviving objections are fixable design points at level 2: maintenance-fit-1 (nothing enforces the worker subtraction), maintenance-fit-2 (whether master takes the same exported symbols as back branches) and standards-compat-1 (the per-backend attribution change in minor releases). Michael Paquier's objection for HEAD is still open in message #21, so a committer who knows the area must decide the shape per branch.

brief.title: Stop parallel worker WAL being counted twice in pg_stat_wal
brief.problem: Since Postgres 14, pg_stat_wal counts WAL written by parallel workers twice, once by the worker and once by the leader through InstrAccumParallelQuery. The author's parallel VACUUM reproducer reports 131% of the WAL actually written. Parallel vacuum, pruning and hint bits set in parallel scans are affected, and so is pg_stat_get_backend_wal().
brief.proposed_design: The leader adds worker counters both to pgWalUsage/pgBufferUsage and to new globals pgWalUsageFromWorkers/pgBufferUsageFromWorkers. Before reporting to cumulative stats, the leader subtracts the worker part using a helper, ComputeOwnWalUsage, and workers keep reporting their own activity. EXPLAIN and pg_stat_statements keep reading the combined pgWalUsage.
user_visible_surface: pg_stat_wal stops counting parallel worker WAL twice.
pg_stat_get_backend_wal() for a leader stops including its workers' WAL, about 31MB less in one reviewer's test.
C API: new exported globals pgWalUsageFromWorkers and pgBufferUsageFromWorkers in instrument.h; a reviewer asked to make them static.
author_claims: The bug exists since pg_stat_wal arrived in Postgres 14 and has a reproducer.
The fix has no performance impact, because the subtraction runs at stats flush and not in a hot path.
The fix is simple enough to backpatch to all branches.
The same approach can later replace pgStatBlock(Read|Write)Time with diffs of pgBufferUsage for pg_stat_database.
brief.thread_state: Bertrand Drouvot and Andres Freund accept approach (1) for back branches, but Michael Paquier objects that pgWalUsage should not contain worker data and prefers a leader-only counter, at least on HEAD. Lukas plans a v2 with Bertrand's comments and a commit message saying the pg_stat_get_backend_wal() change fixes attribution.
unclear: No v2 is posted, so the brief does not know whether the new globals become static or which comments get added.
The thread does not settle whether master takes the same fix or waits for the stack-based instrumentation rework.
The patch adds no regression test, and reviewers chose not to insist on one.
The material does not say whether the backpatch adds exported symbols to stable branches, which matters for ABI.
The commit message mentions buffer statistics, but the material does not say whether any buffer-based cumulative stats change now.

prior_attempts.title: Parallel leader process info in EXPLAIN output
prior_attempts.quote: I think this is doubling down on a fundamentally wrong decision to have ExecParallelRetrieveInstrumentation do some aggregation immediately.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane objected that 0001 adds another field to every PlanState and builds on ExecParallelRetrieveInstrumentation aggregating data early, so it should instead return raw leader and per-worker data for explain.c to aggregate. He also said it was unclear how the leader output maps to non-text formats without breaking which fields are present. The author dropped 0002 because of other refactoring work, agreed 0001 needed a rewrite, and marked the entry returned with feedback.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P7 added leader-only EXPLAIN output and a PlanState field, not a cumulative stats fix. It shares only the background that worker data is merged into leader state early.

objections.title: Unenforced rule: every pgWalUsage diff for cumulative stats must subtract workers
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch diffs pgBufferUsage to feed pg_stat_database, or adds another WAL-based stats kind, and uses the global directly instead of a ComputeOwn*Usage helper. Parallel worker activity is counted twice again. Nothing fails at build or test time, and users find out from inflated monitoring numbers years later, as happened with pg_stat_wal since version 14.
objections.argument: Message #3 says nothing guarantees the invariant, and the planned guard is a comment in instrument.h (messages #3, #7). The patch adds no regression test, and reviewers chose not to ask for one (message #7). The author already plans the next user of this pattern, buffer timing for pg_stat_database (message #1), so the same trap gets a second consumer soon.
objections.author_must_show: What makes a future patch that diffs pgWalUsage or pgBufferUsage for cumulative stats, without the worker subtraction, fail in a test or at review instead of in the field?

critic.reasoning: The hazard predates the patch, but message #3 confirms that nothing enforces the rule and the only planned guard is a comment. Message #1 plans a second user of the pattern for pg_stat_database, so the scenario is concrete.

objections.title: Master gets exported API the author calls an interim workaround
objections.failure_scenario: Master ships ComputeOwnWalUsage() and pgWalUsageFromWorkers/pgBufferUsageFromWorkers, and an extension starts using them. Stack-based instrumentation then removes or redefines them one release later, and the extension breaks. Meanwhile pgBufferUsageFromWorkers is accumulated on every parallel query but no stats consumer reads it yet.
objections.argument: The author calls approach (1) "ugly" and a step before a more elegant solution in the stack-based thread (message #20). Michael objects to it on HEAD as an abuse of pgWalUsage (messages #13, #21), and Andres says the stack-based work removes the main problem with approach (2) (message #17). Back branches may need approach (1), but master could take a leader-only design or a fix with no new exported symbols. [P3] reverted a parallel instrumentation fix that "doesn't seem to be the best possible fix".
objections.author_must_show: Why should master take the same exported globals and helper as the back branches, instead of a static-only fix or the leader-only design that the stack-based work allows?

precedents.title: Revert "Fix accumulation of parallel worker instrumentation."

critic.reasoning: Michael's objection to approach (1) on HEAD is still open in message #21, so the question stands. [P3] gives no usable reason and must not be used as support, and an extension break at a major release is a weak scenario.

objections.title: Backpatch removes parallel worker WAL from per-backend stats with no replacement
objections.failure_scenario: A monitoring tool samples pg_stat_get_backend_wal() for a long-lived session that runs parallel VACUUM. After a minor release, that leader's wal_bytes drops by about a third in message #22's test. The worker WAL now shows up in no per-backend entry at all, because each worker's entry is dropped when it exits.
objections.argument: On stable branches, pg_stat_get_backend_wal() counts worker WAL once, in the leader's entry (message #22). The pgstat_backend.c hunk is an attribution change, not a double-counting fix, and message #23 and message #24 agree on that. It matches the documentation, but it moves WAL out of the only per-backend view that showed it, and message #24 leaves a per-leader worker view to future work. Fixing pg_stat_wal does not need this hunk, so a committer would likely ask why a reporting change goes into minor releases with the bug fix.
objections.author_must_show: Why should the pg_stat_get_backend_wal() attribution change go to stable branches rather than only to HEAD, where a per-leader worker view could come with it?

critic.reasoning: Messages #23 and #24 justify the change by the documentation, but they do not discuss stable branches. After a minor release, worker WAL appears in no per-backend entry, and the thread leaves the replacement to future work.

refuted.title: Patch adds compensating state instead of separating worker data on HEAD
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch, such as the planned pg_stat_database change in message #1, diffs pgBufferUsage for cumulative stats and does not call the subtraction helper. Parallel worker activity is then counted twice again. Nothing fails, and users find out only when someone compares the stats against real activity, as happened here after Postgres 14.
refuted.argument: [P7] was returned partly because worker data was aggregated into leader state early, and the reviewer did not want new code built on that. v1 keeps the same early merge into pgWalUsage and adds pgWalUsageFromWorkers plus a subtraction to undo it at report time. Message #3 states that nothing enforces the invariant, and messages #13 and #21 call the merge an abuse of pgWalUsage. Message #17 accepts approach (1) only for back branches, so a committer would likely ask why HEAD should take it too.
refuted.author_must_show: On HEAD, what makes a future cumulative-stats user of pgWalUsage or pgBufferUsage fail loudly if it skips ComputeOwnWalUsage, rather than double count silently?

precedents.title: Parallel leader process info in EXPLAIN output

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1, which states the same unenforced invariant without relying on [P7]. [P7] concerned a new PlanState field and EXPLAIN output, and the HEAD question is covered by maintenance-fit-2.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: instrument.h gains exported globals pgWalUsageFromWorkers and pgBufferUsageFromWorkers and the function ComputeOwnWalUsage(), also on stable branches.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The author proposes a backpatch to all branches, which changes pg_stat_wal and pg_stat_get_backend_wal() values in minor releases.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every future cumulative-stats user of pgWalUsage or pgBufferUsage must subtract the worker part, and only a comment guards that rule.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: InstrAccumParallelQuery does extra additions per worker; the subtraction runs only at stats flush.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What makes a future patch that diffs pgWalUsage or pgBufferUsage for cumulative stats, without the worker subtraction, fail in a test or at review?
Why should master take the same exported globals and helper as the back branches, instead of a static-only fix or the leader-only design?
Why should the pg_stat_get_backend_wal() attribution change go to stable branches, where no per-backend entry shows worker WAL afterwards?
Does the backpatch add exported symbols to stable branches, or will v2 make pgWalUsageFromWorkers and pgBufferUsageFromWorkers static?
Does any buffer-based cumulative statistic change with this patch, or is pgBufferUsageFromWorkers accumulated with no reader yet?

committability.owner_note: Andres Freund and Michael Paquier take part in the thread but disagree on the shape for HEAD. The owner needs to know the cumulative stats code and parallel instrumentation.
committability.liability: The owner signs for changed pg_stat_wal and pg_stat_get_backend_wal() numbers in minor releases on all branches since 14, and for new symbols in instrument.h that the stack-based instrumentation work may later change.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answers reviews within a day, plans a v2 with Bertrand's comments, and works on the related stack-based instrumentation thread.

priority.reason: The patch is about 10 KiB in four files and fixes wrong pg_stat_wal totals for anyone running parallel vacuum or parallel scans. The open points are the shape on HEAD and the scope of the backpatch, which a v2 and the engaged committers can settle.

provisional_note: Only 3 of 24 messages and no code were read, and v2 is not posted. The review could not check whether the new globals are static, how the pgstat_backend.c hunk behaves, or whether every InstrAccumParallelQuery caller is covered.

precedents_retrieved.title: speeding up GIN build with parallel workers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch splits a GIN index build between parallel workers, each scanning a range of heap blocks and building its own rbtree of entries. The workers send sorted entries through shared memory to the leader, which merges them and writes each key once; the leader later also takes part as a worker.
precedents_retrieved.objection: In April Robert Haas moved it to the next CommitFest because it had too little review and too few comments. He also found no parallel-safety check for expression indexes, workers opening the heap and index with no lock, and no agreement on the gin_shared_mem GUCs. Michael Paquier returned it with feedback mainly because of Heikki Linnakangas's suggestion to keep the rbtree but flush it to tapes and merge them with the tuplesort.c machinery from Peter Geoghegan's parallel B-tree patch.
matched_queries: parallel worker WAL statistics double counting
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If we flushed the tree to a tape instead, then we could perhaps use the machinery that Peter's parallel B-tree patch is adding to tuplesort.c, to merge the tapes.

precedents_retrieved.title: logicalrep_worker_launch - counting/checking the type limits
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes logicalrep_worker_launch() so it checks only the worker limit for the type being launched: the tablesync limit for tablesync workers and the parallel apply limit for parallel apply workers. It also applies the same garbage-collection retry to parallel apply workers that tablesync workers already get, and fixes a copied comment in logicalrep_sync_worker_count().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after a long period without activity. Amit Kapila asked whether the garbage-collection condition could be reproduced and whether a crashed leader worker would restart the server anyway, and the author never answered. The entry moved to Waiting on Author, and the author withdrew it when the commitfest manager asked him to answer or withdraw.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow setting parallel_workers on partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow the parallel_workers reloption on partitioned tables, so that the planner uses it to choose the number of workers for a Parallel Append over the partitions. A later version also let grouping relations take the setting from the partitioned table they read, for partitionwise aggregation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley questioned the semantics: a high setting on the partitioned table can request more workers than the partitions use, and the number does not shrink when the planner or run-time pruning removes partitions. Laurenz Albe and Amit Langote agreed the design needed more thought, and Amit Langote suggested a separate parallel_append_workers option. The thread then stalled, the patch stopped applying, and Daniel Gustafsson marked it Returned with Feedback.
matched_queries: parallel worker WAL statistics double counting
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If someone sets the partitioned table's parallel_workers high so that
they get a large number of workers when no partitions are pruned
during planning, do they really want the same number of workers in
queries where a large number of partitions are pruned?

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallelize correlated subqueries that execute within each worker
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build parallel plans for queries with correlated subplans when each subplan runs entirely within one parallel worker, so no Param value has to pass between workers. After review, the design changed to treat PARAM_EXEC params as parallel safe by default, track required params on each rel, and insert a Gather node only where that set is empty.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread shows no author reply after Tomas Vondra's July 2024 review, and the entry was returned with feedback in October 2024. That review found that regression tests failed on a changed plan in select_parallel, reported a compiler warning, and listed code comments. It also said no reviewer was able to confirm that the PARAM handling is correct.
matched_queries: parallel worker WAL statistics double counting
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And in general the patch looks reasonably simple and clean, but my knowledge of PARAM intricacies is pretty much nil, so I'm hesitant to claim the patch is correct.

precedents_retrieved.title: system load consideration hook for parallel workers
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Tom Lane, Peter Geoghegan
precedents_retrieved.summary: Before starting parallel workers, check the current system load and reduce the number of workers when the system is busy, so parallel query does not slow down other sessions at peak load. The author proposed a hook for this and later posted a POC patch that measures CPU load and picks the worker count from the free CPUs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut argued that a load-based control for parallel workers alone is premature before there is field experience with parallel query, and that the problem covers all process types. He also did not trust system load metrics as a gatekeeper, since load averages lag by about a minute, and found the POC code platform-specific and poorly documented. He suggested refining the existing process-count settings instead, and closed the entry as not favored by the community.
matched_queries: parallel worker WAL statistics double counting
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We don't yet have enough field experience with the parallel query
facilities to know what kind of use patterns there are and what systems
for load management we need.  So I think building a highly specific
system like this seems premature.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PG19]pg_dump --statistics restores extended statistics by attribute number
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_dump --statistics writes extended statistics (ndistinct, dependencies) with the source table's attribute numbers, which can be invalid or point to other columns after restore. The patch passed source column numbers and names to pg_restore_extended_stats and remapped them by name; v2 only rejected the data when the column names did not match.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier said name-based mapping has its own problems, such as a column renamed to a former column's name, and that the logical vs physical attnum issue is old and not worth dozens of hours. Corey Huinker said the restored stats are overwritten by the next autovacuum and that rejected stats are caught by vacuumdb --missing-stats-only. On v2, Michael Paquier doubted the inheritance-child case happens in practice and saw nothing worth acting on, so the author withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I mean that there is nothing that I see worth acting on here.

precedents_retrieved.title: Get rid of pgstat_count_backend_io_op*() functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the pgstat_count_backend_io_op*() functions, so I/O counters are incremented once, and copies the pending I/O stats into the per-backend pending stats when the I/O stats flush. To make this work, per-backend stats must flush after the other stats kinds, first by placing PGSTAT_KIND_BACKEND last in the enum and later (v3) by flushing it outside the loop in pgstat_report_stat().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected to the ordering dependency between stats kinds at flush time, which so far have been independent, and said the copy approach hurts readability. He also said there was no benchmark data to choose among inlining, static structures, copies or fewer diffs, so the picture was incomplete. Andres Freund rejected the alternative WalUsage-style diff approach as too costly. The thread ends with the author disagreeing, and the visible messages do not show a final decision.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Hmm.  I really have an issue with the ordering dependency this
introduces between stats kinds, assumed to happen inside the code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert support for improved tracking of nested queries
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert support for improved tracking of nested queries
Reverted commit(s): Track more precisely query locations for nested statements; Fix regression with location calculation of nested statements; pg_stat_statements: Add tests for nested queries with level tracking
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts the two following commits:
- 499edb09741b, track more precisely query locations for nested
statements.
- 06450c7b8c70, a follow-up fix of 499edb09741b with query locations.
The test introduced in this commit is not reverted.  This is proving
useful to track a problem that only pgaudit was able to detect.

These prove to have issues with the tracking of SELECT statements, when
these use multiple parenthesis which is something supported by the
grammar.  Incorrect location and lengths are causing pg_stat_statements
to become confused, failing its job in query normalization with
potential out-of-bound writes because the location and the length may
not match with what can be handled.  A lot of the query patterns
discussed when this issue was reported have no test coverage in the main
regression test suite, or the recovery test 027_stream_regress.pl would
have caught the problems as pg_stat_statements is loaded by the node
running the regression tests.  A first step would be to improve the test
coverage to stress more the query normalization logic.

A different portion of this work was done in 45e0ba30fc40, with the
addition of tests for nested queries.  These can be left in the tree.
They are useful to track the way inner queries are currently tracked by
PGSS with non-top-level entries, and will be useful when reconsidering
in the future the work reverted here.

roaster_notes.note: For back branches no precedent argues against approach (1), and message #17 sees no alternative there. The one objection above concerns HEAD only.

pg_stat_wal and pg_stat_statements semantics stay as users expect, and pgWalUsage keeps its meaning for extensions. From this angle, only the per-backend attribution change in back branches raises a concern.

The fix changes only backend-local instrumentation counters and the values flushed to cumulative stats. It changes no on-disk format, stats file layout, WAL record, catalog, or wire protocol. The back-branch ABI risk is small: v1 adds two exported globals and keeps the meaning of pgWalUsage and the signature of InstrAccumParallelQuery. Bertrand suggests making the globals static, which removes even that risk.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes how a leader subtracts worker WAL counts before flushing to pg_stat_wal and pg_stat_get_backend_wal(), and it adds no new view, function, role check or data path, so no user can see or do anything new. Whether the new exported globals affect ABI belongs to other angles.
The bug is real and the fix is cheap at flush time, so the objections are about long-run upkeep and the shape of master.

This is a bugfix for wrong numbers in pg_stat_wal and pg_stat_get_backend_wal(). No existing feature, setting or extension stops the double counting. Users can only compare pg_current_wal_lsn() deltas by hand, and that does not fix the cumulative view. A second mechanism (rubric item 12) is out of scope here because the patch fixes an existing mechanism, and the design dispute between the in-thread alternatives belongs to another angle.

This is a bug fix. pg_stat_wal reports about 131% of the WAL that parallel VACUUM writes, and both message #1 and message #22 reproduce it. Every user who reads pg_stat_wal while parallel vacuum or parallel scans run sees the wrong totals, so the demand angle has nothing to object to. Design disputes, such as whether pgWalUsage should hold worker data (messages #6 and #13), belong to other angles.
